qt: to the Commission Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

On 28 September 2026, the Italian Government called on the Council of EU Agriculture Ministers, to release funds from the EU agricultural reserve to finance exceptional measures aimed at addressing serious market disturbances (private storage of olive oil) and providing swift support to operators in the sector. According to the relevant letter, closing stocks at European Union level for the period 2025-2026 are estimated at around 420 000 tonnes, a higher volume compared to previous periods1. The excessive accumulation of olive oil reserves is tangible proof of the difficulty the international market is having in absorbing olive oil production. At the same time, it is putting significant pressure on producer prices, with a possible further increase in supply drastically squeezing the profit margins of olive oil producers2. Given the gravity of these developments, the critical nature of the sharp drop in producer prices for olive oil, as well as the need to support and protect sector operators, can the Commission say: Has the Greek Government or any other government submitted a similar request to that of the Italian Government, for funds to be released from the European Union’s agricultural reserve?
